text:
Anna (PM): quick sync — customer X wants hard tenant isolation + cross-region failover. they asked for explicit routing policies and an SLA. can we surface what we need to commit to for q3?
Raj (Staff Arch): what do they mean by "hard" isolation? full dedicated GPUs per tenant or logical isolation via slices?
Anna (PM): they said 'no co-tenancy on inferencing GPUs' and KMS-controlled keys for model artifacts. also regulatory: traffic must terminate in eu-west only.
Carla (Eng Lead): full dedicated infra is heavy. we can offer customer-dedicated pools (Redwood Dedicated) but will need capacity reservation and pricing.
Devon (SRE): ops concern — dedicated pools across regions means separate failover model. we need runbooks for cross-region evacuation and capacity drain.
Helen (Sales): customer budget is modest; asking for dedicated capacity + low-latency eu region SLA. they expect launch in 6 months.
Mike (Infra): question — do we allow routing fallback to a nearby region if eu is unhealthy? that would violate their data residency ask.
Raj (Staff Arch): two options: 1) strict geo-containment: requests never leave region — simpler contract but more expensive. 2) geo-failover with data-escape policy + customer approval — cheaper but more compliance risk.
Anna (PM): let's capture launch criteria proposals so we can negotiate: availability target (99.9?), max p95 latency, cost delta for dedicated pool, and acceptable data residency fallback policy.
Carla (Eng Lead): from tech side: minimum TODOs: 
- model pinning support per-customer pool
- tenant routing rules with region affinity + no-evacuation flag
- per-tenant KMS integration + audit logs
- provisioning pipeline for dedicated GPU pools (terraform module)

I'll estimate effort after we pick a policy.
Raj (Staff Arch): additional infra requirements: control-plane separation (tenant-scoped config), routing policy DSL update, and telemetry tagging for tenant isolation billing.
Devon (SRE): runbook items: automated warmup, graceful eviction hooks, priority preemption rules, and a playbook for cross-region disasters. need canaries for webrtc/streaming tests.
Helen (Sales): customer asks for canary SLA for first 30 days and an option to downgrade to logical isolation if cost becomes prohibitive.
Mike (Infra): provisioning time for dedicated pool ~4-6 weeks with current capacity. autoscale burst could be enabled but we'd need quota increases.
Anna (PM): propose we offer two SKUs to customer X: 
- SKU A: Strict Regional Dedicated — no egress, pinned model versions, SLA 99.95 for p50/p95 latency, price premium.
- SKU B: Tenant-Sliced (soft isolation) — shared pools with KV/prefix caching isolation, geo-failover allowed with consent, lower price, SLA 99.9.

Which of these is feasible for a Q3 commitment?
Carla (Eng Lead): SKU B is doable with engineering runway ~8 weeks if we prioritize routing + caching isolation work. SKU A requires dedicated provisioning automation and KMS integration — realistically 12-16 weeks.
Raj (Staff Arch): risks for SKU B: noisy neighbors on long-sequence workloads; need robust prefix caching and token budgets per-tenant.
Devon (SRE): ops impact: SKU A increases maintenance windows (per-tenant). need dedicated oncall rotations for large customers.
Anna (PM): launch acceptance criteria draft: 
- Functional: tenant routing policy enforced, per-tenant model pinning, KMS keying for artifacts, and audit logs hooked into console.
- Performance: p95 latency within target SLA under expected load profile.
- Reliability: automated fallback behaviors defined and tested (canary + blast radius limits).
- Ops: provisioning < 6 weeks for standard dedicated SKU, documented runbooks, SLO alerts and runbook drills.

Raj (Staff Arch): also require a migration path for customers moving from SKU B -> SKU A and back. include data transfer cost visibility.
Helen (Sales): we'll push for SKU A at a higher price, but they want an option to start with SKU B. this maps to a canary rollout product motion.
Mike (Infra): dependency list: quota increases, marketplace images for private deployment, terraform modules, and KMS onboarding checklist.
Carla (Eng Lead): action: I'll run a rough effort breakdown and put JIRA epics for routing-DSL, pool-provisioner, kms-integration, and telemetry. will have numbers by EOD Friday.
Anna (PM): action: I'll draft the customer offer and launch acceptance criteria doc and sync with legal for data residency language.
Devon (SRE): action: I'll draft runbooks and schedule a DR drill for the new failover modes.
Helen (Sales): I'll communicate the two-SKU option and timing to customer X and confirm their minimum commit window.
eng-bot: deploy status — canary pipeline healthy, no blocking deploys in this workspace.
Anna (PM): next sync Wednesday 11:00. please add any missing risks/comments here. :thumbsup:
Raj (Staff Arch): risk note: cost model for SKU A needs to include long-tail GPU idle time; propose billable reserved hours.
Carla (Eng Lead): +1 to billable reserved hours. also need acceptance test harness for latency under multi-tenant stress.
Helen (Sales): customer will expect tooling to show billing impact before they sign. we need a simple calculator for committed capacity.
Anna (PM): good call — added to action list. thanks everyone.
